text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 billing exceeds what this panel's complexity predicts in every complexity band, but records came back for too few claims to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel does skew complex, and 99215 share rises with condition count as expected, yet this provider's 99215 share is roughly two to four times the all-provider share within each complexity band, including patients with zero or one condition. That means case mix alone does not appear to explain the excess. Sampled low-complexity 99215 claims such as C0085924, C0085976 and C0085999 (J06.9 upper respiratory infection only) and C0086143 (N39.0 urinary tract infection only) are the kind of visits where a top-level code is hardest to justify. The documentation signal points toward unsupported billing: 2 of 3 documented 99215s fell below the billed level, including C0085753 with low MDM and even the complex-patient claim C0085805. However, three documented 99215s is far too thin a base to lean on, and only one supported 99215 (C0086307) is available for contrast. A reviewer should first request charts for a targeted set of low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the acute single-diagnosis visits listed above, and check documented MDM and time against the billed level."}
